articles.title: Bill Oddie Reflects on Rochdale Roots in BBC Documentary
articles.excerpt: Bill Oddie, the renowned television presenter and comedian, explored his family history in Rochdale during an episode of Who Do You Think You Are?
articles.content_html:
Bill Oddie, the television presenter and comedian known for his work on The Goodies and Springwatch, revisited his Rochdale roots in a recent episode of the BBC show Who Do You Think You Are?. Born at Birch Hill Hospital in Littleborough in 1941, Oddie moved away from Rochdale at the age of seven when his father secured a job in Birmingham.

During the programme, Oddie discovered that his ancestors were all mill workers, with his grandmother Emily Worrall likely working in Arrow Mill in Castleton from the age of 13. He reflected on his childhood, noting a distant relationship with his father and the impact of his mother's mental health struggles on his upbringing.

Oddie's mother, Lilian, was committed to a psychiatric institution when he was young. He believed she suffered from schizophrenia and abandoned him, only seeing her a few times before her death in 1990. However, he learned through the documentary that she had been diagnosed as manic depressive and had experienced significant trauma, including the loss of two children.

The exploration of his family's history prompted Oddie to reassess his feelings towards his mother. He expressed regret for his previous harsh judgments, stating, "This journey has been a real lifesaver... I wish I'd known her better and I wish she'd had a better life." Oddie passed away on Saturday at the age of 85.
